src.t.1xmyesr: It stalled at a red light that was not even there. Where is my petrol?
src.t.11zwqp6: Is it broken? It is not moving. It was moving yesterday. Wait, was it?
src.t.1j2f45k: It cleaned the garage, found the dock and left my sock alone. I want one in every office. In my office. Only mine.
src.t.8z69ux: Mostly clean. Mostly alive. Mostly not eating the cables.
src.t.16jlgbf: It cleaned a third of the garage and ate my phone charger. Strategic, I assume.
src.t.v6o8kh: A robot that goes round in circles and plays sad music. I could have hired an intern.
src.t.w90fok: I put my face on a tea glass. It looks like I was born there. How much do we charge a month for this?
src.t.buntqv: My moustache blurred into the wall. Fix that and then, a subscription.
src.t.1ab10q4: The scratch is still there, and now so is a smear. Is this the “before” photo?
src.t.188jxut: My face is green. The tea is blue. Is this modern art or a bug? Both are billable.
src.t.1fvpahn: I zoomed in on the tea glass until I could see the glaze. It was still smooth. I want to zoom in on my ego next. Add that.
src.t.1v3ynas: The logo is lovely until you zoom in. Please make it so nobody zooms in.
src.t.1f1z0y1: My tea glass has corners. Glasses do not have corners, Rıza says. I did not ask Rıza.
src.t.yf9kdo: The letter O is solid, the star is a hexagon and the file is bigger than the video site. Impressive, in a way.
src.t.33je4n: I am on a beach. I am in 4K. I am a genius. Export it before I wake up.
src.t.1dqezej: The beach is nice. Why is my suit green on one side?
src.t.y6p4pb: My lips say “synergy” and my voice says it a second later. Like a bad dub.
src.t.zvpdmi: This is not an editor. This is a slideshow with opinions.
src.t.1fmmaaj: The tea arrived warm, the drone came home, and nobody was scalped. I will call this my idea.
src.t.zs07n4: It flew. It delivered something tea-adjacent. The glass is half what it was.
src.t.7ad4oa: The drone delivered tea to the ceiling. Then the ceiling to the floor.
src.t.58fhll: This is not a drone, this is a very expensive ceiling fan with ambitions.
src.t.8irs87: I’ll take the ground station. Radios are just very slow WiFi, right?
src.t.f1ymql: I’ll do the sensors. Gyro plus accelerometer, how hard can two liars be.
src.t.ditffc: Open the 📋 board. Code tasks are on the laptop, the bench stand and the ground station are on the rack.
src.t.1io8rkt: Four, so it can steer by speeding some up and slowing others down. Tip it right: speed up the left pair. Nose down: speed up the rear pair.
src.t.shmu3x: And two spin clockwise, two counter-clockwise, because a spinning prop twists the body the other way, like me stirring a tea and the glass wanting to turn. The twists cancel; speed one pair up to turn on purpose.
src.t.1ita9vs: The mixer is just who does what for each command. One sign wrong and the drone does the opposite of what it is told, which at five hundred times a second is over very quickly.
src.t.geg6xn: Two witnesses. The gyro says how fast you turn; add that up and you have the angle. Smooth, but it has a tiny constant error, so after a minute it is sure you are upside down.
src.t.m34d50: The accelerometer feels where gravity pulls. Right on average, but jumpy, and when the drone itself speeds up it cannot tell a push from a tilt. Like tea slopping in a glass when the bus brakes: it thinks the table is tilted.
src.t.1eiic1a: So: trust the gyro for the quick part, the accelerometer for the slow part. A complementary filter does that with one number. A Kalman filter does it with maths, and also learns the gyro’s error.
src.t.qrfcsj: Because the motors hum at about a hundred and twenty-five times a second and shake the chip. Gossip with a lawnmower going in the background.
src.t.fa59ty: A notch filter removes only that one hum and costs almost nothing. A low-pass smooths everything but makes the signal late, and late is dangerous in a loop that corrects five hundred times a second.
src.t.9keg0o: If the hum gets through, the D term amplifies it and the motors jitter and get hot. You can measure that in degrees on the motor.
src.t.2u5wrg: P pushes in proportion to the error: the further off, the harder. I remembers errors that stay, D reacts to how fast the error is changing and calms things down.
src.t.d048fq: Two loops: the outer one says how fast to turn to reach the angle, the inner one pushes the motors to turn at exactly that speed. Like telling someone “head for the door” and then them adjusting each step.
src.t.1xv1svh: Turn the gains up and it reacts faster, until the delays catch up: the motor lag, the speed controller’s update rate. Then it overshoots, corrects too much, and rings.
src.t.1utke7j: And on the pad: the integrator adds up the error while the drone sits tilted and cannot move. At take-off it empties it all at once. That is windup.
src.t.1jsvfg2: The camera sits on two little servos that turn against the drone, like carrying a tray while the floor rocks.
src.t.9n01nh: Feedback alone only reacts after the camera has already moved. Feed-forward knows the drone’s tilt and moves the servos at the same time. Both together is best: the first does the work and the second tidies up.
src.t.16iowhi: It is a thin pipe, about three and a half thousand bytes a second. Telemetry goes down it, and so do the heartbeats that tell the drone the ground station is alive.
src.t.50ndqk: Ask for fifty updates a second and the pipe is full. Packets drop, heartbeats too, and after a few seconds the drone decides the link is dead and flies home, in the middle of the delivery. Ten a second is plenty to watch.
src.t.lx2jsl: It decides by itself. No heartbeat for a few seconds: fly the route back and land at home. Battery low: go home while there is still some left to get there. Reach the fence round the boss’s office: turn around.
src.t.1cg6lsh: Wait too long to give up and the battery is gone before it is home. Wait too short and a lost packet sends it home for nothing. Hovering sounds safe, until the battery runs out and it lands in the ceiling fan.
src.t.18heilm: Sensors in, motors out, five hundred times a second. The ground station watches and has the failsafes. Don’t let it near the office.
src.t.1eu95r3: The IMU is a tiny chip with a gyro and an accelerometer. The gyro says how fast you turn, the accelerometer says which way gravity pulls. Like a waiter with a very good inner ear.
src.t.1jll532: Both are shaken by the motors’ hum, so we filter them first, but every filter makes the signal a little late.
src.t.1ivyddy: Two liars, one angle. The gyro is smooth but wanders off; the accelerometer is right on average but jumpy, and fooled whenever the drone itself accelerates.
src.t.nog4ze: The estimator takes the gyro for the quick part and the accelerometer for the slow part. Get the mix wrong and it believes it is level while it is not.
src.t.yp5a1d: The outer loop asks: how far am I from where I want to lean? It answers with how fast to turn.
src.t.7163ty: Too gentle and the drone is lazy; too keen and it overshoots like a waiter with a full tray.
src.t.1dvu0b4: The inner loop is fast and does the actual work: it compares how fast we are turning with how fast we were asked to, and pushes the motors to close the gap.
src.t.55kt7x: D damps the ringing but also amplifies the hum, which heats the motors.
src.t.1lf7q3j: Three commands and a throttle become four motor speeds. To roll right, the left motors speed up and the right ones slow down.
src.t.mdtj32: Two props spin each way so their twisting pushes cancel. Yaw is just speeding up one pair and slowing the other.
src.t.n8l00w: Each motor has an ESC, a speed controller. How often it hears a new command matters: old PWM listens fifty times a second, DShot thousands.
src.t.178nbr0: And a motor takes a moment to speed up. All that delay is why the gains cannot be turned all the way up.
src.t.1l6r5ww: The camera sits on two little servos that turn against the drone’s tilt, like carrying a glass of tea while the floor rocks.
src.t.16xxr5t: It does best when it knows what the drone is about to do (feed-forward) and also checks what the camera really sees (feedback).
src.t.10ry6pr: The ground station is the laptop screen you fly it from: the map, the buttons, the mission. It refuses to arm a drone nobody has calibrated on the bench.
src.t.53pdel: A thin radio carries telemetry down and heartbeats up. Ask for too much telemetry and it clogs, the heartbeats go missing and the drone thinks the link is dead.
src.t.mx8amp: When no one is at the controls, the drone decides for itself. No heartbeat for a few seconds: go home. Battery low: go home while there is still some. Reach the fence round the boss’s office: turn around.
